summary: In major commercial space developments, Rocket Lab has formally protested NASA's decision to award a $700 million Mars orbiter contract to rival Blue Origin, despite Rocket Lab recently conducting a dedicated orbital launch for a secret customer. On the defense front, the U.S. Space Force selected Texas to host a site for the trinational Deep Space Advanced Radar Capability network, targeting operations in 2030, while Poland announced plans to develop a national satellite communications constellation. In civil policy, NASA issued a request for information to establish a United States Space Academy and confirmed that Djibouti will become the latest signatory to the Artemis Accords, expanding international data-sharing efforts. Commercial industry milestones included a $161 million award to Antares for space nuclear power technology, alongside a successful orbital demonstration where two private spacecraft maneuvered within 650 feet of one another. In scientific developments, researchers released an open-source AI model trained on 17 years of lunar data, published a new surface atlas of Phobos to support Japan’s upcoming MMX sample-return mission, and presented preliminary analysis of 3,000 supernovas suggesting dark energy may be evolving. Looking ahead, readers should watch for NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 team as the astronauts prepare to brief the public on their ongoing space station mission and plan their upcoming return to Earth.
